disease_label_per_paper: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome-associated acute kidney injury after olanzapine dose increase
presentation_summary: 31-year-old man with schizophrenia had olanzapine increased from 5 mg to 10 mg daily during psychiatric admission.
After 5 ward days he developed fever 38.9 C, restlessness, confusion, generalized rigidity, tachycardia, and tachypnea.
CK was 256020 U/L and serum creatinine was 766.9 umol/L, consistent with severe rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI.
He required urgent intermittent hemodialysis, bromocriptine, lorazepam, and withdrawal of antipsychotic therapy.
Symptoms and labs improved over roughly two weeks and he was discharged well.

risk_context.source_text_value: Olanzapine was being administered before deterioration.
Olanzapine dose was increased from 5 to 10 mg daily.
Severe rhabdomyolysis and AKI required aggressive hydration and dialysis.

quality_warnings: The paper diagnosis is preserved but not used as ordinary ranking evidence.
Ordinary ranking evidence emphasizes olanzapine exposure and dose increase, fever, rigidity, confusion, tachycardia, tachypnea, extreme CK, and AKI requiring hemodialysis.
